Pulmonology · published research

Pneumonia

A 30-person randomized trial reported shorter hospital stay and improved oxygen saturation, inspiratory pressure, forced vital capacity, and symptoms with 940-nm LED PBM plus standard care. A 2022 report from the same registered program described blood-count outcomes in 21 patients.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

A 30-person randomized trial reported shorter hospital stay and improved oxygen saturation, inspiratory pressure, forced vital capacity, and symptoms with 940-nm LED PBM plus standard care. A 2022 report from the same registered program described blood-count outcomes in 21 patients.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Respiratory system > Pneumonia category contains three titles: two human PBM reports and one mouse photodynamic-therapy paper. The human reports share trial registration UTN U1111-1229-1296. Their samples differ in reported size, and overlap is unresolved, so they should be treated as one registered program rather than two proven independent trials.

Human and clinical evidence

The 2022 prospective blinded descriptive report included 21 people, with 11 receiving infrared LED PBM plus conventional therapy and ten receiving conventional therapy alone. It focused on blood components during community-acquired pneumonia treatment (Pereira et al. 2022). A 2026 randomized trial reported 30 patients and found shorter hospital stay, higher oxygen saturation, improved maximal inspiratory pressure and forced vital capacity, and reduced respiratory symptoms when 940-nm LED PBM was added to antibiotics and physiotherapy (Pereira et al. 2026). Both cite the same trial registration, so the reports may share participants.

Animal evidence

The category contains one mouse photodynamic-therapy paper. Photodynamic therapy activates a photosensitizer and is distinct from the PBM interventions assessed here, so it is not counted as PBM pneumonia evidence.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone cell or ex-vivo PBM study is listed for pneumonia.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The 2026 clinical report used a 940-nm infrared LED vest alongside conventional treatment. Wavelength is the light's color band and affects how far light can travel through tissue. The article did not provide a common dose that can be compared across other pneumonia protocols in the database.

Interpretation

The randomized result is clinically relevant but comes from one small registered program with possible overlapping publications. Independent trials should replicate respiratory outcomes, hospital stay, and safety before the effect is treated as established.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow for short-term hospital recovery outcomes from adjunct 940-nm LED PBM in one small randomized report Very low for independent replication because two human papers share one trial registration and may overlap
Publications and records3 titles (exact Respiratory system > Pneumonia)

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

One small randomized report describes improved recovery with LED PBM added to standard care, but a 2022 blood-count paper shares the same trial registration. The patient samples may overlap. Larger trials with transparent enrollment and independent replication should confirm respiratory and hospital outcomes.
